mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes under these conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months, coupled with falling industrial production (INDPRO), indicates a deteriorating labor market and reduced economic output, which predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 6.5% for 2 consecutive months AND INDPRO declines for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly below zero in at least 80% of triggered periods (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 1% while the unemployment rate is below 5% signals an inflationary supply shock, which typically precedes positive equity returns as central banks prepare to tighten policy and markets anticipate higher pricing power.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% during a period of negative GDP growth (GDPC1) signals an emergency easing, which boosts risk asset valuations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly above zero in at least 75% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 60% of triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 3% while consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is below 2% suggests households are accumulating cash rather than spending, which typically precedes a slowdown in consumption-driven growth and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in at least 65% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.7% for three consecutive months, with no corresponding rise in unemployment (UNRATE < 5%), signals an expansionary supply response that boosts earnings expectations and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change > 0.7% for 3 consecutive months AND UNRATE < 5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
